Ankle

Point-and-flex work to wake up stiff ankles. Sit or hold support so you cannot lose balance.

Good to know

Ankle sprains recover with early gentle movement and balance practice, not weeks of stillness unless advised. If you cannot bear weight, or swelling is major after an injury, get assessed.

Before you start

Do any of these apply to you right now?

  • Chest pain, pressure or tightness
  • Trouble breathing or shortness of breath
  • A recent fall, accident or blow to this area
  • Fever, or feeling generally unwell
  • New numbness, weakness, or bladder/bowel changes
  • Recent surgery on this area
  • Unexplained weight loss or pain that never eases
  • The worst headache of your life, fainting, or slurred speech

None of these apply — you can continue to the exercises below.

These need a person, not a web page. If any of them describe you, do not use the exercises today.

Start slowly — perform only the movements your physiotherapist reviewed with you.

Exercise

Ankle pumps

Repeat
15 times
Sets
2
Start
Sit in a firm chair with the sore heel resting on the floor, toes pointing up.
Move
Slowly point your toes away from you, then pull them back toward your shin.
Direction
Full slow range both ways — point, then flex, like pressing and releasing a pedal.
Return
Each flex back to the start completes one repetition.

Target: Calf and shin muscles that move the ankle.

Stop with cramping that does not ease or any sharp pain.

Exercise

Toe raises

Hold
3 sec
Repeat
12 times
Sets
2

Hold 3 seconds — a timer appears here.

Start
Stand tall holding a sturdy chair or counter, feet flat on the floor.
Move
Keeping your heels down, slowly lift the front of both feet off the floor.
Direction
Toes rise toward the shins — hold the support lightly for balance.
Return
Hold briefly, then lower the forefeet slowly back down.

Target: Shin muscles that lift the foot when walking.

Keep support in reach — stop if balance feels unsafe.

Important notice — read before exercising
